content.text:
I've finished reading. Here's what I'd tell my son.

---

"Hello, sweetheart. The short version is that I didn't decide anything. I'm not moving a single shekel until you or the bank explain it to me, and I'm sure about that.

It's a page about Harel, black background. Under 'כל המוצרים של הראל' it lists everything they have: תגמולים, קרן השתלמות, קופת גמל להשקעה, קרן חדשה מקיפה, קרן חדשה כללית and חיסכון לכל ילד. The one already chosen was 'קופת גמל להשקעה', 16 tracks. Nowhere does it say פיקדון or anything with a fixed interest rate. So the thing I came for, something as safe as my deposits that gives more, isn't on this page.

**The cost.** It says 'דמי ניהול ... מ־0.54% עד 0.61%' from 'החיסכון', and '0%' from 'ההפקדה'. At first I thought '0% ההפקדה' meant the deposit earns nothing. Then I understood it's probably what they take from what you put in. I'm not sure. Lower down it says the law allows up to 1.05% and 4%, so it seems they take less than the maximum. That calmed me a little.

**How it has done.** On most of the rows it doesn't say. It says 'פחות מ־3 שנים' again and again. Where there are numbers, the biggest one I saw was 'מניות' with 24.04% for 3 years. That's shares, and that's exactly what burned me with the adviser. There's one called 'כספי (שקלי)' with 4.25% for 3 years and 3.08% for 5 years. It sounds like money in shekels, but I don't know what it means or whether it's as safe as a deposit. Also, the small print says the return is before management fees and before tax, and that it doesn't say what will happen later.

I didn't understand: S&P 500, 'עוקב מדד', 'מט"ח', the little coloured circles, 'PF-10', and 'הלכה יהודית' as an investment track.

The small grey lines at the top and under the table were hard to read even enlarged. At the end there's a list of things that fold open, like 'קרנות מחקות', 'קרנות סל' and 'מה כתוב במסמכים של הראל'. I didn't open them.

What wore me out was that every row repeats the same things: 'ההחיסכון', 'ההפקדה', 'מניות', 'מט"ח', the yellow and green dots, 'פחות מ־3 שנים'. I had to read all of it again on each row just to find the one number that was different. By the middle of the table I was tired. So many numbers on a black screen made me anxious.

So, will you come over and look at it with me? Or I'll ask at the bank."
